comments.author: pluma
comments.story_title: “Swift will be open source later this year”
comments.why_zh: 被引作“程序员抗拒更好的语言”这一说法的出处
comments.text_zh: 但程序员并不想要更好的语言[0]。程序员大多只想要他们已有的东西。光靠说“看，这是一门更有趣、更现代的语言”，你是没法克服这种抵触的。程序员嘴上说想要更好的语言，但你要仅凭一门新语言本身的优点说服他们切换过去，祝你好运。Swift 唯一实实在在的好处是，它可以在 iOS 上替代 Objective-C——这对 iOS 很重要，因为 Objective-C 本身就因为语法陌生而构成了更大的门槛。Swift 在 iOS 上能赢，是因为它竞争的是一门本来就没人想学的语言。就算从熟悉度来说，Swift 看上去唯一熟悉的对象（凭第一印象）也只有 Ruby，只不过它用的是更熟悉的类 C 语法（也就是大括号）。虽然 Ruby 程序员极其显眼（尤其是在创业公司/硅谷圈子里），但他们的人数并没有那么多——更别提其中有些人已经转向 Rust 或 JS 了。0：[VIDEO]
comments.text: But programmers don't want better languages[0]. Programmers mostly just want what they already have. You can't overcome that kind of resistance just by saying "look, here's a language that's more fun and modern". Programmers say they want better languages, but good luck trying to convince them to switch to a new language just by its merit. The only tangible benefit of Swift is that it can be used instead of Objective-C for iOS -- which is important for iOS because Objective-C poses an even bigger hurdle by virtue of its unfamiliar syntax. Swift wins on iOS because it competes with a language nobody wanted to learn to begin with. Even as far as familiarity goes, the only thing Swift looks familiar to (based on first impressions) is Ruby, except it uses a more familiar C-like syntax (i.e. braces). While Ruby programmers are extremely visible (especially in startup/valley crowds) there aren't that many of them -- not to mention that some have already moved on to Rust or JS. 0: [VIDEO]
